AlgoSB 2026: Learning Protein Dynamics

Dynamic Reweighting for Unbinding Processes

(2) Biased Potential

In this part, the original potential gets biased and used to yield unbinding times which gets reweigthed to estimate the unbinding times or rates for the original potential done previously.

From the previous simulation, we now know the unbinding rate for the chosen cluster and potential parameters. In this idealized case, the unbiased simulation should have progresses fast enough to get a good rate estimation at a decent time. However, higher unbinding rates should also require shorter dynamics runs and, thus, should be quicker to compute. Here, the previous initial cluster setup is loaded ( cluster_data = np.load('lj_cluster_init.npz') ) with the same (adjust if needed) potential definition but also an additional bias potential of a 1D LJ potential between the central C and leaving N atom. In case of the same σ parameter value, the sum of two LJ potentials between the same atoms yields one LJ potential with an effective ε parameter value formed by the sum of both. VLJ = 4ε [ ( σ r ) 12 - ( σ r ) 6 ] +4ε' [ ( σ r ) 12 - ( σ r ) 6 ] = 4(ε + ε') [ ( σ r ) 12 - ( σ r ) 6 ] Thus, by assigning a negative ε value in the bias potential, the binding strength between C and N is lowered. TASK Modify the cluster potential by a bias to reduce the binding strength between the C and N atom significantly (e.g. half or less than the original potential). The effective atom pair potential will be plotted below after a initial structure minimization and potential scan along the C-N distance.
